hero.subtitle: When a faulty product injures someone in Camarillo, the path to accountability doesn't have to start with a lawsuit against a stranger's carelessness. California's strict liability rules focus on the product itself, and our team can help you understand how to build that kind of case.

about.title: Camarillo Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Camarillo residents rely on countless everyday products — from appliances used near Ponderosa Drive shopping centers to auto parts and safety equipment used on trips along US-101. When one of those products fails because of a design flaw, a manufacturing error, or a missing warning, the injuries that follow can be sudden and serious. California law generally allows injured people to pursue a strict liability claim, which means the focus stays on whether the product was defective rather than on proving a manufacturer acted carelessly. That distinction matters, because manufacturers, distributors, and even retailers in the supply chain may share responsibility. If you or someone in your Camarillo household was hurt by a product that didn't work the way it should have, we can review what happened and what options exist at no cost. There's never any obligation to move forward.

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Path
items.desc: Because California often applies strict liability to defective products, you may not need to prove the manufacturer was negligent — only that the product was defective and caused harm.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which widens the pool of who may be accountable for what happened to you.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters
items.desc: Our team can advise you early on how to safely keep the product involved, since it often serves as key evidence in showing the defect that caused your injury.

items.question: What should I do with the product that injured me?
items.answer: Try not to alter, repair, or discard it, and keep it in the condition it was in when the injury happened. Packaging, manuals, and receipts can also help us evaluate the claim. We can advise you on safe storage until it's reviewed.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California's strict liability framework generally focuses on whether the product itself was defective — in design, manufacturing, or warnings — rather than requiring proof of negligence. We can explain how this applies to your specific situation.

items.question: Does it matter that I live in Camarillo specifically?
items.answer: Where you live can affect which court has jurisdiction and which local resources or records are relevant, such as retailers along Las Posas Road or purchases made near US-101 corridors. Our team familiar with Ventura County matters can help sort through those details.

items.question: Is there a cost to talk to us?
items.answer: No. Our initial case review is free, and we typically work on contingency, meaning there's generally no fee unless there's a recovery. Reaching out simply starts a conversation with no obligation.
